answer: By constructing a spectral graph partition barrier, a knoll-like structure is formed around each cluster of nodes, isolating them from one another and preventing trust propagation across the graph. This is achieved through personalized EigenTrust matrices, which attenuate the influence of adversary nodes, much like a karst landscape erodes the connectivity of an adversary bridge, rendering it impassable to trust diffusion. As a result, clusters of honest validator nodes are rapidly isolated from one another, ensuring asymptotic consensus convergence and Sybil resistance.
